concepts.def: A push or pull, measured in newtons (N).
Mass (kg) is matter; weight (N) is the gravitational force, W = mg.
The single force equivalent to all forces acting.
Relate force, mass and motion (F = ma).
Rate of change of velocity; a = F ÷ m.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hang a weight on a spring - it stretches. Double the weight, double the stretch.

This is Hooke's Law: extension is proportional to force, up to the elastic limit.

Past the elastic limit, the spring stays stretched and won't bounce back.

Drop a skydiver. Gravity pulls down, air resistance pushes up.

At first, gravity wins - they accelerate. As they get faster, air resistance grows.

Eventually forces balance. They fall at a constant terminal velocity.

Opening a parachute increases air resistance, forces unbalance, they slow down to a new safe terminal velocity.

A free-body diagram shows all forces on one object as arrows.

Arrow length = size of force. Arrow direction = direction of force.

For a swimming fish: weight down, upthrust up, thrust forward, drag back. If they all balance, the fish swims at constant speed.

mcqs.q: Why does a skydiver eventually fall at constant speed?
options: Gravity disappears
Air pushes harder than gravity
Gravity and air resistance balance
They run out of mass

mcqs.q: Past the elastic limit a spring will.
options: Always return to shape
Become permanently stretched
Get heavier
Lose its mass

mcqs.q: Is radioactive decay periodic — does each nucleus decay at regular intervals?
options: No — decay is a random process; half-life is a statistical property of a large population.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
Yes — each nucleus 'ticks' at intervals of one half-life until it decays.
Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Elastic limit”?
options: Point where spring stops returning to shape.
Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.
Arrow showing direction and size of a force.
Push of a surface, perpendicular to it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Upthrust”?
options: Push of a surface, perpendicular to it.
Arrow showing direction and size of a force.
Constant max speed during a fall.
Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Normal force”?
options: Arrow showing direction and size of a force.
Point where spring stops returning to shape.
Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.
Push of a surface, perpendicular to it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hooke's Law”?
options: Extension of a spring is proportional to force.
Arrow showing direction and size of a force.
Point where spring stops returning to shape.
Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Terminal velocity”?
options: Constant max speed during a fall.
Push of a surface, perpendicular to it.
Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.
Point where spring stops returning to shape.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Force arrow”?
options: Upward force from a fluid on an object in it.
Extension of a spring is proportional to force.
Arrow showing direction and size of a force.
Push of a surface, perpendicular to it.

mcqs.q: A spring stretches 2 cm per 1 N. If you hang 6 N on it (within the elastic limit), how much does it stretch in cm?
